newsitem.title: UK: C&W locked in divorce talks with Veba.
newsitem.headline: C&W locked in divorce talks with Veba.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Plc, Britain's second biggest telecomes operator, was on Wednesday locked in talks with its German partner, utility company Veba AG, about the future of their joint investments in Germany and Europe.
"Discussions are continuing," a company spokesman told Reuters, declining to comment further on what the two groups were discussing or when a statement might be expected.

C&W looks set to abandon its two-year, strategic alliance with Veba, called Vebacom, which was set up in 1995 to compete against German telecoms giant Deutsche Telekom after continental European phone markets are liberalised around 1998.

Industry sources have said that C&W has begun to balk at the scale of infrastructure investment required and fears it would not have enough management control of the new company, which also took German utility RWE AG on board last year.
Spending too much money on Vebacom could hamper plans to expand C&W's new cable giant, C&W Communications, that it has formed with three other cable companies.
The sources said the firm planned to make the development of this company a leading plank of its European strategy.
Veba sources say the German group has offered to buy C&W's 45 percent stake in Vebacom and analysts are speculating that the price is the chief obstacle to ending the alliance.
C&W paid 1.92 billion marks for its Vebacom stake and the Financial Times said the UK company wanted full restitution of its investment.

Veba sources also say C&W wants to buy back Veba's 50 percent share in their joint venture called C&W Europe, which provides voice and data telecommunications to business customers in European countries such as France, Italy, Spain, Ireland, Portugal, Belgium and Switzerland.
C&W Europe, in which C&W has the management lead, employs about 400 staff around Europe. Worldwide, Cable and Wireless has a total of 40,000 employees.
